title: Added dissector for the Monero wire protocol
description:
Initial version. PDU reassembly plus parsing the header only.
The data payload is still presented as raw bytes.

notes.body: offset is never read after this - generates a clang warning.  Maybe comment this line out?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13522/diffs?diff_id=864038479&start_sha=52af9e72e7768c8b0e1b49acbeff8c10dc2babb2#31e7d1a556887f95779f050e207831ee568532bc_127_126)
Commented out.
No need to separately fetch this, if use proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint() at line 114.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13522/diffs?diff_id=864038479&start_sha=52af9e72e7768c8b0e1b49acbeff8c10dc2babb2#31e7d1a556887f95779f050e207831ee568532bc_120_120)
Done.
Maybe add another 'unknown' field here to highlight when bits are set that dissector doesn't handle yet? Up to you.
Could you point me to a dissector in which it is implemented like that?

All I meant was that if you don't know what is in these other flags, maybe add the remaining bits in this 32-bit field as an 'unknown' or 'reserved' field, just to make it more visible if some of them are set in captures you are looking at.  The remaining bits could have a mask of 0xfffffff0.  As I said, up to you.

Yeah I was mostly wondering whether I can set the mask like that.

All these other bits are reserved and not used at the moment, having said that I have decided to follow your advice, the protocol tree looks better imo when nothing is hidden from the user, even if it's just plenty of zero bits.
Will this preference really ever get switched off?  Could get same effect by turning reassembly off in TCP dissector..
It's a standard design pattern though...
True
Ok so I am leaving it as it is then.
